title: Impact Sale of State Land on Reserves and Accounting Treatment of Cost of State Land for Public Housing
what_it_is: Impact Sale of State Land on Reserves and Accounting Treatment of Cost of State Land for Public Housing

sections.label: HDB land cost and subsidies
sections.summary: Questions ask whether Singaporeans pay triple for state land in HDB flats and whether HDB will give cost and subsidy breakdowns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance whether Singaporeans are paying (i) the cost of state land used for public housing when initially acquired by the Government (ii) the difference between the higher land cost when the land was purchased by HDB for development, and that which the Government initially acquired the land for and (iii) taxes to cover the shortfall incurred by HDB from the land cost paid to past reserves at full market price, thereby amounting to triple payments for use of state land that are developed into HDB flats if the land acquisition and development occurred in two different terms of Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development in view of the POFMA Correction Directions issued on 14 October 2022 to an individual for his Facebook posts dated 4 October 2022, whether HDB will provide (i) a clear breakdown of the total development cost of all new flats henceforth and (ii) the value of the "generous subsidies" applied to the assessed market price of these new flats.

sections.label: State land as reserves
sections.summary: Under the Constitution, all state land forms part of Singapore's reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Under the Constitution, all state land forms part of our reserves.

sections.label: Reserves invested for NIRC
sections.summary: The $1 million cash is part of reserves invested through GIC, with up to 50% of long-term expected real returns used yearly as NIRC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The $1 million cash now forms part of our financial reserves, which the Government invests, for example, through GIC, to grow for the benefit of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We use up to 50% of the long-term expected real returns on the investment every year in our annual Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This amount is known as the Net Investment Returns Contribution or NIRC.

sections.label: No net reserve increase
sections.summary: Selling state land converts a physical asset to a financial asset, so there is no net increase in reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Again, it would be a conversion of a physical asset to a financial asset to make up for the state's loss of use of the land for the period of that carving out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Thus, the answer to Mr Leong's first question is: (a) There is no net increase in the reserves when state land is first sold and the sales proceeds are transferred to the financial assets.

sections.label: BTO discounts and EHG
sections.summary: Singaporeans buy BTO flats below fair market value, and eligible first-timer buyers can get the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant of up to $80,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: (c) Singaporeans buy BTO flats at a discount from their fair market value and in addition, eligible first-timer flat buyers can enjoy the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG) of up to $80,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh asked whether, in view of the POFMA Correction Direction issued on 14 October 2022, HDB will provide a breakdown of the total development cost of BTO flats and the value of the subsidies applied to them.

sections.label: HDB Homeownership Programme deficit
sections.summary: HDB's financial statements show flat sale proceeds are less than building and grant costs, with a $3.85 billion FY2021/2022 deficit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The financial statements contain information on the costs incurred in its Homeownership Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They show that the total amount that HDB collects from the sale of flats is less than the cost of its building programme and the housing grants it disburses each year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For the Financial Year (FY) 2021/2022, HDB recorded a deficit of $3.85 billion in its Homeownership Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The average deficit incurred by HDB in the last three years, FY2019/2020 to FY2021/2022, was about $2.68 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Because the question that was asked by the Leader of the Opposition in his Parliamentary Question (PQ) was in view of the POFMA Correction Directions issued, whether HDB will provide a breakdown.

sections.label: Government subsidises flats before sale
sections.summary: The Government states that flats are generously subsidised before they are sold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The correlation is the Government's point that flats are generously subsidised before they are sold.

sections.label: POFMA economist and HDB subsidies
sections.summary: The speaker notes the POFMA-ed person was GIC's chief economist and hopes the Minister answers on an HDB subsidy breakdown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The connection would be that the identity of the individual who was issued the POFMA Correction Direction – I cannot name him by virtue of Standing Orders, but he was the chief economist of the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, if the Minister says that this has been known for a long time, one would expect someone of that stature to also not fall afoul of POFMA and be POFMA-ed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But I think the Minister has said that she will answer that question – so, I hope the Minister can answer that question on whether HDB will provide a breakdown of the subsidies.

sections.label: POFMA post on HDB loss
sections.summary: The POFMA-ed post alleged a disingenuous and misleading analysis of HDB's $270 million loss.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The chase is this: the POFMA-ed post alleged that there was a "disingenuous and misleading analysis" of the $270 million loss made by HDB.

sections.label: HDB losses and net loss figure
sections.summary: The speaker says HDB losses were always known, and Minister Desmond Lee's POFMA Clarification gave the net loss.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The fact that when we build HDB flats under the housing programme, the fact that the Government incurs losses, that is known and was always known, even before Mr Yeoh posted it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But coming back to the question that the Leader of the Opposition has asked, the reason why I say there is no correlation is this: it is because what Minister Desmond Lee gave in the POFMA Clarification was the net loss.

sections.label: Nothing achieved by doing so
sections.summary: The answer is that nothing would be achieved by doing so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The answer is that we do not think that anything would be achieved by doing so.

sections.label: Not helpful or meaningful
sections.summary: The straightforward answer is that it would not be helpful or meaningful to do so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: My straightforward answer is that it would not be helpful or meaningful to do so.

sections.label: PLH flat subsidy recovery
sections.summary: PLH flat buyers selling after the 10-year MOP must return additional subsidies as a percentage of original assessed market value, based on resale price.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: An HDB PLH flat buyer, upon selling his PLH flat after the 10-year MOP, will have to return the quantum of additional subsidies provided as a percentage of the original assessed market value of the flat; and the subsidy recovery will apply to the resale price that is a reflection of the prevailing market value, regardless of whether the flat is sold at a gain or a loss.

sections.label: HDB resale price increase
sections.summary: Median price of 4-room and larger HDB resale flats rose 26% between 2017 and 2022, reaching record highs and pushing up land market price.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The median price of a 4-room and larger HDB resale flats has increased 26% between 2017 and 2022, with resale prices reaching record highs today and, therefore, pushing up the market price of land.

sections.label: BTO price-to-income ratio
sections.summary: HDB states price-to-income ratio for non-mature estate BTO flats is around five or less, with about 25% of salary for mortgage servicing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: HDB states that the price-to-income ratio for BTO flats offered in non-mature estates is around five or less, which means the purchase price is around five times one's annual income, or around 25% of one's salary is set aside for mortgage servicing.
